Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: Mosslume original resident four-direction STANDING design source atlas, transparent PNG, 2 columns x 2 rows.
Input image 1 is the approved four-person original concept lineup. Use ONLY the specified resident; all other people must be absent.
Input image 2 is the approved protagonist's four-view game-character design. Use image 2 ONLY for the SAME small game-sprite body proportions, camera elevation, pixel-cluster style and optical body height, NOT for its protagonist identity or costume.
Exactly four full-body views of ONE resident, in this exact reading order: TOP LEFT front/down toward viewer; TOP RIGHT profile facing RIGHT, nose pointing right; BOTTOM LEFT back/up away from viewer with NO face or eyes; BOTTOM RIGHT profile facing LEFT, nose pointing left.
Friendly cozy top-down/three-quarter pixel-game character, approximately three-head proportions like image 2, clear silhouettes and deliberate square pixel clusters, simplified clothes detail, warm neutral matte lighting. Maintain SAME head/body size, hair volume, costume and local foot baseline across all four views. Relaxed empty hands at sides; all equipment attached to belt rather than held in hands. Preserve anatomical accessory placement when rotating.
Composition: square canvas with four equal invisible square cells, one centered whole body per cell, generous transparent padding around hair, hands and boots. Character crown near 15% cell height, planted soles near 87%, consistent local foot anchor. No clipping. No grid lines, separators, frames, lettering, names, text, extra people, scenery, ground, drop shadows, colored halos, glow, watermark or background. Genuine alpha transparency everywhere except the figure. This is four poses, NOT a crowd or motion sequence.
Resident identity: SECOND person from left in image 1, the young adult female farmer. Copper/auburn hair in one thick side braid, warm sun-touched medium skin, cream collared rolled-sleeve shirt, sage green work overalls/trousers, ochre-yellow practical apron tied at waist, small seed pouch at belt, brown cuffed work boots. Keep same warm face and gentle competent mood. Braid rests over anatomical RIGHT shoulder in front view and is visible on the corresponding side/back views. No basket, tools, produce or hat. Slim-to-average sturdy working build; same optical height as protagonist.

Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: Mosslume transparent inventory MATERIAL icon source atlas, 4 columns x 3 rows, exactly TEN distinct original material icons and TWO empty transparent slots.
Input image 1 is the approved seven-tool icon atlas. Match ONLY its deliberate chunky low-resolution pixel clusters, dark outlines, warm wood/metal shading and consistent three-quarter item angle. No tools from that image should appear.
Exact cell reading order:
TOP ROW: 1 bark-covered short LOG with visible cut growth rings; 2 chunky grey STONE with broad matte facets; 3 green/dried PLANT FIBER bundle tied with simple twine; 4 small stack of three flat light-brown sawn PLANKS.
MIDDLE ROW: 5 two or three earthy red-brown CLAY lumps, smooth and matte; 6 rough grey COPPER ORE rock with clearly orange copper flecks; 7 rough grey IRON ORE rock with dark silvery iron veins, NO orange flecks; 8 one refined orange-copper rectangular COPPER BAR ingot with bevels.
BOTTOM ROW: 9 one refined cool grey-silver rectangular IRON BAR ingot with bevels; 10 black lumpy COAL with subtle charcoal-grey edges; 11 EMPTY; 12 EMPTY.
Design every icon to be clear at logical 32x32. Each item fits comfortably within its own invisible square cell with balanced optical scale and ample transparent gutters. Raw ores look irregular and rough, smelted bars look regular and manufactured; stone, clay and coal must have different shapes and values. Neutral soft matte light, restrained highlights, no neon or magical glow.
Wide 4:3 canvas. Exactly 10 isolated icon subjects in the listed cells; bottom row last TWO cells remain completely alpha transparent. Genuine alpha-transparent background and gutters. No grid, dividers, tile frames, labels, numbers, letters, text, shadows, ground, hands, scenery, extra icons or watermark.

Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: Mosslume original farm crop growth-state SOURCE atlas, transparent PNG, 3 columns x 2 rows, six different sequential states of ONE crop.
Input image is a visual-style reference for the island world ONLY: use the same compact top-down/three-quarter 2D pixel look, plump distinct leaf clusters, dark green outlines, lime/yellow-green highlights and dense readable shapes. Do not reproduce any island, building, tree, interface, character or text from the reference.
Use neutral evenly lit base textures: no night illumination baked in. Deliberate crisp square pixel clusters, simple limited color groups, clean dark outline, suitable for logical 32x32 world sprites, magnified for source-art review. Not watercolor, vector clipart, realistic botany, smooth 3D or a farming infographic.
Composition: 3 columns by 2 rows of six equal invisible square cells. Same camera, SAME WORLD SCALE and root point across all six states, root point at (50% cell width, 82% cell height). Size must GROW naturally between states: do not enlarge seeds or seedlings to fill the cell. Mature plant fits within about 75% of cell height and width, with clear transparent padding. Crop alone with at most a tiny root-contact soil speck; no square soil tile, no large soil platform, no flowerpot, no below-ground cutaway, no ground shadow. Every cell contains exactly one planted clump/state. Genuine alpha-transparent backgrounds and gutters. No grids, frames, divider lines, captions, lettering, numbers, arrows, text, watermark or extra plants. Stages are game states, not all the same full-grown plant recolored.
Crop: WHEAT. Exactly six states in reading order:
1 SOWN: three tiny wheat grains partially nestled in a tiny dark-brown root-contact mark, no green leaves.
2 SPROUT: very small two-leaf bright green seedling, about one fifth mature height.
3 YOUNG: compact tuft of 4-5 upright slender green blades, about two fifths mature height.
4 GROWING: several taller green jointed stems with small green unripe ear tips, about three quarters mature height.
5 RIPE: full clump of 4-5 curved golden wheat ears and ochre stalks, obvious grain kernels, a few green basal leaves; tallest state, harvest-ready, no basket or loose bundle.
6 HARVESTED: short cut tan stubble, 3-4 clipped stalk ends at the same root point, no ripe ears.
All six states retain ONE shared plant base/root anchor. Mature wheat logical height about 24 pixels, harvested stubble about 5 pixels.
